brief.headline: Cut ₹28.69 L/yr by matching Mars Plastics & Premier Plastic prices on the three big SKUs, and win 15-day faster payment (worth ₹8.01 L cash freed up) by offering to pay them in 30 days instead of 45.

priceAsk.summary: Match the Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic prices on the three main SKUs — that alone closes ₹28.69 L/yr of overpay.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.81/NOS on the 28 mm PP cap (we pay ₹1.08, Mars is ₹0.81); ₹1.38/NOS on the 30 mL HDPE bottle (we pay ₹1.53, Mars is ₹1.38); ₹0.35/NOS on the measuring cup (we pay ₹0.46, Premier is ₹0.35).
priceAsk.basis: We already buy identical rigid plastic items cheaper from Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic. The open market ask for the 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — so ₹0.81 is fair and achievable. Closing these three gaps saves ₹28.69 L/yr.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days — or go even tighter to 30 days if they cut another ₹8.01 L off the price (the value of paying 15 days faster).
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying in 30 days instead of 45 frees up ₹16.02 L cash for us; paying 15 days faster than 30 (if they agree) frees another ₹8.01 L.

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is small — ₹4.11 Cr in sales — and we're nearly half of it at ₹1.95 Cr (47.43%). They keep only 6.0% profit on every sale, much less than similar firms (15.0%), so price cuts hurt them more than most. They owe 1.13× their own cash and their cash is stuck for 101 days, so they value faster payment. They already take 39 days to pay their own suppliers, longer than similar firms (23 days), so asking them to let us pay in 30 instead of 45 is fair. Their financial health is middling (51/100, grey zone on the distress score of 1.83), so push firmly but don't squeeze so hard you risk their ability to deliver — line up a second source first.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹28.69 L/yr versus the cheapest price we already get
We're 47.43% of their entire revenue — huge buying power
They keep only 6.0% profit, well below peers at 15.0%
They take 39 days to pay their own suppliers, longer than similar firms at 23 days
Paying them in 30 days instead of 45 frees up ₹16.02 L cash for us
Market ask for the 28 mm cap is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — a proven, strong second-source for exactly what we buy.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed, ₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health 73/100)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — robust and profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: We're 47.43% of their sales — losing us would devastate them, but it also means they may struggle to absorb a big price cut and still deliver reliably; qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek before you push hardest.
Their distress score is 1.83 (grey zone) and health only 51/100 — if you squeeze too hard, supply could wobble; focus on payment speed (which helps their cash) alongside the price ask.
They're very small (₹4.11 Cr) — verify they can scale if our volumes grow, and that quality holds at the lower price.
They owe 1.13× their own cash — a modest supply risk if credit tightens; keep an eye on delivery performance and have the backup ready.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but right now we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more than we do for the same items from Mars and Premier — let's close that gap and talk about how paying you faster can help your cash flow.
